title: Factoring vs. self-funding a freight brokerage
seoTitle: Factoring vs. self-funding a freight brokerage
searchIntent: Should a freight broker consider factoring with cash available?
excerpt: Compare funding costs with billing, credit checks, collections and the time required to manage a brokerage’s cash flow.
takeaway: Compare factoring with the full cost of managing receivables yourself, including administration and credit risk. Having enough cash does not settle whether the service is worth its price.

sections.title: Should a freight broker consider factoring with cash available?
paragraphs: Luis asks a useful question in this lesson: are you comparing a financing fee with the actual alternative, or only with the balance in your bank account? Self-funding still requires someone to approve credit, gather paperwork, invoice customers, collect payment and reconcile the records.

An established brokerage with an accounting team may handle that work differently from a new owner doing everything alone. The decision depends on your transaction volume, customer mix, staff and the terms offered by the provider.

sections.title: List the work that comes with the money
paragraphs: Ask which services are actually included. Credit screening, invoice processing and collections may have limits, separate fees or responsibilities that remain with you. Get a clear description before assigning value to them.

Then list what you currently spend in time and money to perform the same work. If a provider takes over a task, decide how you will use the time released. Paying for convenience only helps the business when the service is reliable and the benefit is real.

sections.title: Compare costs over the same period
paragraphs: An invoice-based factoring fee and an annual borrowing rate are different measures. Compare the actual dollar cost for the expected collection period, including minimum fees, additional charges and any reserves.

The rates discussed in the original recording are historical examples. Use a current written proposal and your own receivables history. A customer that regularly pays later than expected can change the economics of either approach.

sections.title: Read the risk terms before relying on the label
paragraphs: Recourse, nonrecourse and credit protection are not interchangeable promises. Read which events are covered, what disputes are excluded and when repayment or repurchase obligations can arise. Also review termination, customer notification and control of collections.

Luis’s operating perspective is to consider the whole business, not just the financing line. Build a side-by-side comparison and review the contract with your accountant or qualified adviser before committing. No funding arrangement removes the need to manage cash and customer risk.
